/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 29 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2670 (-7)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4283 (-21)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1979 (13)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1534 (-8)
Baltic Handysize Index: 811 (7)
CAPESIZE
A slightly mixed tone to close the day, with activity skewed toward the Pacific while the Atlantic remained comparatively subdued. The BCI 182 5TC slipped by $196 to settle at $38,843, masking a firmer underlying tone in parts of the market. In the Pacific, sentiment continued to improve, supported by a more active cargo flow and the presence of four miners on C5. Rates edged higher, with the index nudging up by $0.040 to $13.240. It was a notably date-sensitive market, with a clear premium for earlier arrivals, fixtures were reported at $13.50 for 12 May ETA, easing back to the $13.10–$13.15 range for mid-May dates. The tightening tonnage list in the basin, coupled with steady miner and operator participation, underpinned the positive tone. In contrast, the Atlantic remained somewhat standoffish despite signs of underlying support. The C3 index held broadly stable, inching up $0.055 to $33.173, with the ballaster list for May loaders still tight. However, a lack of bids was noticeable, whereas offers were said to be closer to $34 on index dates.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market is said to still be under supplied for trans Atlantic stems resulting in market rates and subsequent fixture levels slipping. Although to contradict this, brokers said a stand-off was appearing. Fronthaul is reported to be more active today, especially from North Coast South America and it has also been said that there have been some split Atlantic Cape stems feeding down into the Panamax market. The P1A dropped by $132 to $13,768 and the P2A also slipped by $146 posting at $24,433. In Asia, there has been a healthy number of reported coal fixtures from Australia along with Indonesia with a positive sentiment still surrounding the Pacific market. Period activity appeared to be quiet today and the P5TC posted an increase of $119 to $17,814.

Atlantic
Messrs Olam were reported to have taken the scrubber fitted Golden Forward (81,130 2020) open in Cartagena 1 May for a trip via North Coast South America and Turkey redelivery Gibraltar at $16750, although it is unknown how the scrubber benefit was split.

Asia
The Pacific Hibiscus (82,877 2025) Dafeng 29/30 April was reported to have fixed for an Indonesian round trip basis delivery passing Taichung with some suggesting the rate to be sub $23,000 and the charterer remained unknown. Rb Eden (81,067 2016) open in Dalian 4/5 May fixed a stem from Australia into Japan at $21,250 to Mol. Although details are lacking, it was said the Ocean Artemis (93,103 2011) open Mariveles 3/4 May was fixed. Uming covered their Indonesia to Taiwan 7 May stem and Samjoo also covered their North Pacific 17/26 May grains stem, but further clarity was lacking for both.
SUPRAMAX
With holidays taking place in Asia and the widespread Labour Day holiday coming up at the end of the week, unsurprisingly it was a rather slow affair today in both basins. The Atlantic lacked much fresh impetus, although some felt that better levels were being discussed from the US Gulf to Singapore-Japan, however no fixture information surfaced. In Asia very little fresh enquiry was seen both in the north and south as most contemplated the long weekend ahead. The Ultralaz (64,043 2018) open Tianjin was heard fixed for a trip to Sri Lanka with intention slag at $23,000 by HSSC. The 11TC average finished down $96 at $19,391.
HANDYSIZE
It was a mixed day of activity, with minor fluctuations observed across both basins. The BHSI increased by 7 points to 811, while the 7TC average rose by $130 to $14,597. The Continent and Mediterranean markets experienced a relatively quiet session, with underlying fundamentals remaining weak across most loading regions. In contrast, the US Gulf and South Atlantic continued to benefit from fresh enquiry, which is gradually pushing rates above previous levels. Meanwhile, the Pacific market maintained steady activity, with firm conditions supported by a limited supply of available tonnage.

Atlantic
The Laoura (38,552 2017) was reportedly fixed for a trip from Recalada to the Mediterranean at $25,000. The Lady Margaret (31,864 2013) was also fixed on voyage terms from South Brazil to the Mediterranean, though further details have not been disclosed. The Summer Sea (35,240 2013) was heard fixed for an Annaba to Malaysia trip at around $10,500–$11,000 by Norden, with no additional details reported.

Market Fundamentals
EU Sanctions Target Russian Coal Export Routes

The EU’s 20th sanctions package adds the Russian ports of Murmansk and Tuapse, alongside Indonesia’s Karimun oil terminal, to its restrictions. Murmansk handled 1.7 Mt of coal exports in 1Q26, all of which were thermal, down from 2.7 Mt last year, representing around 5% of Russia’s seaborne coal exports, as reported by McCloskey. Turkey accounted for 80% of these shipments. Tuapse volumes declined from 0.9 Mt in 1Q25 to 0.2 Mt in 1Q26, with all shipments of thermal coal this year and Turkey accounting for almost 75% of shipments. The EU has not imported Russian coal since 2022, while rail costs and longer distances make Murmansk less competitive than eastern routes.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve continues to find support despite a weaker Pacific market and surging oil prices. The biggest move was on the May contract with 35500 paid, followed by 33450 pays on Jun. The May v Jun roll widens and strengthens further up to +2100. Q3 was volatile and active with prints between 29700-30400 while the Q4 struggled for similar liquidity, trading between 29500 and 30150. The May v Q3 spread went through in good volume up to 5100, as well as the Jun v Q3 being legged early on up to 3100. Cal27 was hit down to 25500 early on multiple times, together with the Cal28 down to a low of 22500, before recovering back up to 22700.

PMX
A quieter day for Pmx paper as Geneva Dry draws to a close, with the curve trading broadly flat across the board. May traded at a low of 18800 and was paid up to 19600, once again finishing the day around 19100. Jun traded from 19200 to 19750, while Q3 traded up to 18700, causing the C/P Q3 print at 11200. Q4 held a narrow $150 range, printing between 17150 and 17300. On the back end, Cal27 traded 14500 - 14650, while Cal28 saw a print at 13700. The Index started to move more positive, Avg 5tc +119 to $17814.

SMX + HANDY
A lacklustre day of trading in the SMX market, as the curve traded sideways and value floated marginally higher, trading within a tight ~$200 range. Liquidity was focused to the prompt months, May trading 17000 – 17200 and Jun trading 17050 – 17250. While some trading activity also on the back end of the curve, Q3 trading 16300 – 16450, Q4 at 15250, as well as Q1 at 12100 and Q2 at 13900 in small clips. Cal27 traded 12800 – 12850 and Cal28 traded at 12025. Handy Jul traded 14650.

Market Fundamentals
EU Sanctions Target Russian Coal Export Routes
The EU’s 20th sanctions package adds the Russian ports of
Murmansk and Tuapse, alongside Indonesia’s Karimun oil
terminal, to its restrictions. Murmansk handled 1.7 Mt of coal
exports in 1Q26, all of which were thermal, down from 2.7 Mt
last year, representing around 5% of Russia’s seaborne coal
exports, as reported by McCloskey. Turkey accounted for 80%
of these shipments. Tuapse volumes declined from 0.9 Mt in
1Q25 to 0.2 Mt in 1Q26, with all shipments of thermal coal
this year and Turkey accounting for almost 75% of
shipments. The EU has not imported Russian coal since 2022,
while rail costs and longer distances make Murmansk less
competitive than eastern routes.
Trading Commentary
Cape Routes
The route markets again moved higher as oil continued to
push. The c5 may traded a few times from 13.20 to 13.45 in
just over 1m tonnes. The rest of the curve had plenty of
interest but no other trds to report. The c3 also moved
higher with may closing at 33.75 as june closed valued 32.75
with no trades to report.
Cape
The Cape FFA curve continues to ﬁnd support despite a
weaker Paciﬁc market and surging oil prices. The biggest
move was on the May contract with 35500 paid, followed by
33450 pays on Jun. The May v Jun roll widens and
strengthens further up to +2100. Q3 was volatile and active
with prints between 29700-30400 while the Q4 struggled for
similar liquidity, trading between 29500 and 30150. The May
v Q3 spread went through in good volume up to 5100, as
well as the Jun v Q3 being legged early on up to 3100. Cal27
was hit down to 25500 early on multiple times, together with
the Cal28 down to a low of 22500, before recovering back up

Murmansk handled 1.7 Mt of coal exports in 1Q26, all of which were thermal, down from 2.7 Mt last year, representing around 5% of Russia’s seaborne coal exports, as reported by McCloskey. Turkey accounted for 80% of these shipments. Tuapse volumes declined from 0.9 Mt in 1Q25 to 0.2 Mt in 1Q26, with all shipments of thermal coal this year and Turkey accounting for almost 75% of shipments. The EU has not imported Russian coal since 2022, while rail costs and longer distances make Murmansk less competitive than eastern routes. Trading Commentary Cape Routes The route markets again moved higher as oil continued to push. The c5 may traded a few times from 13.20 to 13.45 in just over 1m tonnes. The rest of the curve had plenty of interest but no other trds to report. The c3 also moved higher with may closing at 33.75 as june closed valued 32.75 with no trades to report. Cape The Cape FFA curve continues to find support despite a weaker Pacific market and surging oil prices. The biggest move was on the May contract with 35500 paid, followed by 33450 pays on Jun. The May v Jun roll widens and strengthens further up to +2100. Q3 was volatile and active with prints between 29700-30400 while the Q4 struggled for similar liquidity, trading between 29500 and 30150. The May v Q3 spread went through in good volume up to 5100, as well as the Jun v Q3 being legged early on up to 3100. Cal27 was hit down to 25500 early on multiple times, together with the Cal28 down to a low of 22500, before recovering back up to 22700. PMX A quieter day for Pmx paper as Geneva Dry draws to a close, with the curve trading broadly flat across the board. May traded at a low of 18800 and was paid up to 19600, once again finishing the day around 19100. Jun traded from 19200 to 19750, while Q3 traded up to 18700, causing the C/P Q3 print at 11200. Q4 held a narrow $150 range, printing between 17150 and 17300. On the back end, Cal27 traded 14500 - 14650, while Cal28 saw a print at 13700. The Index started to move more positive, Avg 5tc +119 to $17814. Liquidity was focused to the prompt months, May trading 17000 – 17200 and Jun trading 17050 – 17250. While some trading activity also on the back end of the curve, Q3 trading 16300 – 16450, Q4 at 15250, as well as Q1 at 12100 and Q2 at 13900 in small clips. sections.content: BDI微跌7点至2670，各船型指数涨跌互现。Capesize大西洋表现逊于太平洋，C3持稳而C5走强，5TC录得$196跌幅。Panamax大西洋供应偏紧但出现对峙情绪，亚洲太平洋煤炭询盘活跃。Supramax因亚洲假期因素成交清淡，各航线全线下跌。Handysize美湾和南大西洋需求支撑费率上升。
